The card's all-shifts total for the day: each gap summed over the three shifts and priced once on the day, with each shift's own total beside it (issue #31b review: the server's figure, not the browser's).
A question about shifts 1 and 3: the day total covers those two shifts and their 960 minutes, never shift 2.
Shift 2 holds the refused trim record: it is named in excluded_shifts and left out, and the day is priced over shifts 1 and 3 alone (their gross and 960 minutes), with the excluded record reported.
What waste genuinely costs: each bucket's MSF x paper, plus the run time shear and rejects took.
Where to look: the levers ranked by dollars a year at the post's volumes.
A $40/MSF margin and a 3% trim target: contribution is priced beside, never added, and trim points over 3% become a lever.
Yesterday in the golden window: shift 1's operator downtime is over its 2.5% band.
The most maintenance downtime any shift has: a power outage plus jams; recurrence counts shift 2's own year.
A month: every one of its many flags, each with its own trailing year.
Two flags on shift 3; knife / slitter jam was over its band on its own once in the year, so recurrence is not zero.
The first month in the records: the previous month is outside them, so every previous figure is None, never zero.
The supervisor lens: the controllable losses ranked, schedule-driven trim and planned maintenance unranked.
The ownership lens: the total cost of waste, side trim first.

Against each grade's trailing-year baseline at the usual grade mix (the share of the setup clock over the same year; issue #101): the buckets add up to the gap taken directly, and the grade mix is schedule-driven, never priced.
Against the previous week: each loss is this week's feet below the grade baselines per scheduled minute minus the week before's; an offset bucket is not priced.
Shift 3 against shift 1 over the same week: shift 1's Thursday planned maintenance makes stops an offset; the heavier grade mix of shift 3 is part of its gap.
